t:
(a) 
Section 1512(b)(3) is amended by adding after subparagraph (E) (added by section 112 of this Act) the following new subparagraph:


“(F) 
Conflicts of interest.—No member of a governing body, executive committee, or any entity appointed by a governing body, or executive committee may, in the exercise of any function of the agency described in subsection (e), (f), or (g) of section 1513, vote on any matter before the governing body, executive committee, or any such entity respecting any individual or entity with which such member has (or, within the twelve months preceding the vote, had) any substantial ownership, employment, medical staff, fiduciary, contractual, creditor, or consultative relationship. A governing body, executive committee, and any entity appointed by a governing body or executive committee shall require each of its members who has or has had such a relationship with an individual or entity involved in any matter before the governing body, committee, or entity to make a written disclosure of such relationship before any action is taken by the body, committee, or entity with respect to such matter in the exercise of any function of the agency described in section 1513 and to make such relationship public in any meeting in which such action is to be taken.”.



 
    (b) Section 1524 is amended by adding after subsection (d) (added by section 110(d)(2) of this Act) the following new subsection:


“(e) 
No member of any SHCC may, in the exercise of any function of the SHCC described in subsection (c)(6), vote on any matter before the SHCC respecting any individual or entity with which such member has (or, within the twelve months preceding the vote, had) any substantial ownership, employment, medical staff, fiduciary, contractual, creditor, or consultative relationship. Each SHCC shall require each of its members who has or has had such a relationship with an individual or entity involved in any matter before the SHCC to make a written disclosure of such relationship before any action is taken by the SHCC with respect to such matter in the exercise of any function under subsection (c) and to make such relationship public in any meeting in which such action is to be taken.”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that references to governing bodies, a State Health Coordinating Council, "consultative" relationships and disclosure "public in any meeting" signal outside participation. But the section only adds conflict-of-interest recusal and disclosure rules for members of health planning bodies. It does not create a comment period, hearing, advisory role, consultation requirement, or right to sue tied to a federal decision. It restricts who may vote within those bodies rather than bringing outside parties into a federal decision.

qwen_block.w: This section establishes internal conflict-of-interest rules and disclosure requirements for members of governing bodies and committees. It does not require the federal government to consult or coordinate with outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before making a decision. The 'public' disclosure mentioned is a transparency measure for internal meetings, not a mechanism for public participation or consultation in the decision-making process.
qwen_block.s: A governing body, executive committee, and any entity appointed by a governing body or executive committee shall require each of its members who has or has had such a relationship with an individual or entity involved in any matter before the governing body, committee, or entity to make a written disclosure of such relationship before any action is taken by the body, committee, or entity with respect to such matter in the exercise of any function of the agency described in section 1513 and to make such relationship public in any meeting in which such action is to be taken.
qwen_block.b:
Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the requirement to "make such relationship public in any meeting" constitutes public participation because it involves transparency to the public. However, this is merely a disclosure requirement for internal governance and conflict of interest management. It does not invite the public to comment, advise, or influence the decision-making process itself. The actors involved (members of governing bodies, executive committees, and SHCCs) are part of the administrative structure of the agency (likely Medicare/Medicaid given the context of "SHCC" - State Health Care Commission or similar, and "agency described in section 1513"). Even if these bodies include outside members, the text provided only regulates their internal voting and disclosure protocols, not their interaction with the general public or other outside entities for the purpose of consultation or coordination on a federal decision. The definition requires consultation or coordination *with* people outside the government *before* making a decision. Here, the "public" aspect is just a disclosure of a conflict, not a participatory mechanism. Furthermore, SHCCs (State Health Care Commission) are state-level entities, but the text focuses on the internal rules of these bodies regarding their members' conflicts. It does not describe a process where the federal government consults with them, nor where they consult with the public. It is an internal procedural rule.

Wait, let's look closer. "SHCC" likely stands for State Health Care Commission or similar. The text amends sections regarding "governing body" and "SHCC". The definition says: "Participation is when the federal government may or must consult or coordinate with people outside of the government...". This section imposes rules *on* these bodies. It does not describe the federal government consulting with them. It describes the internal operations of these bodies. Therefore, it is not participation by the federal government with outsiders. It is internal regulation.

Another angle: Are these bodies federal? Section 1512 and 1524 are likely part of the Social Security Act or similar. If SHCC is a State Health Care Commission, it is outside the federal government. But the text doesn't say the *federal government* consults with them. It says the *SHCC* must disclose conflicts. This is a requirement placed on the SHCC. It doesn't involve the federal government consulting with the SHCC. It involves the SHCC's internal procedures. Thus, no federal decision is being made with outside input in this specific text. The text is about conflict of interest disclosures.

Therefore, the label is No.

opus.w: This section only sets conflict-of-interest and disclosure rules for members of state and local health planning bodies (governing bodies, executive committees, SHCCs). It does not create any consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory panel, or right to sue over a federal decision. The 'public in any meeting' language is a disclosure requirement inside non-federal bodies' own meetings, not an opportunity for outsiders to take part in a federal decision. Those bodies' underlying review functions are set up elsewhere in the statute, not here.
opus.s: No member of any SHCC may, in the exercise of any function of the SHCC described in subsection (c)(6), vote on any matter before the SHCC respecting any individual or entity with which such member has (or, within the twelve months preceding the vote, had) any substantial ownership, employment, medical staff, fiduciary, contractual, creditor, or consultative relationship.
opus.b:
I labeled this **No**, with moderate confidence (0.6).

1. **The tempting reading:** This section is about governing bodies, committees and statewide councils (SHCCs) that are outside the federal government. It also mentions public meetings. Some of these bodies review proposed uses of federal health funds. So it can look like outsiders taking part in federal decisions.

2. **Why it fails:** The section only sets ethics rules for those bodies. Members with a conflict of interest may not vote and must disclose the conflict, including at the meeting where action is taken. The section does not create or require any consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory panel or right to sue. The meetings it mentions belong to the state and local bodies themselves, not to a federal agency.

3. **Why I'm not more confident:** The functions these bodies perform under sections 1513 and 1524 may themselves feed into federal funding decisions. If those underlying functions count, a Yes reading is defensible.
